property_summary: For any caller address chosen as the new owner and when called by the admin, the reference contract always sets the public owner variable to that address; the mutant instead overwrites admin so owner != supplied address for some inputs.

For any address newOwner and any admin caller, after admin calls setOwner(newOwner) the public owner() getter equals newOwner in the reference contract; the mutant that omits assignment breaks this because owner remains unchanged.

General rule: when called by the admin, setOwner sets owner to the provided _owner argument (i.e., owner equals the function parameter); the bug breaks this by setting owner to tx.origin instead, so for some fuzzed admin caller and _owner value the resulting owner differs from the provided _owner.

Invariant: Only the original deployer (admin) can successfully call setOwner to change owner; the mutant allowing current owner to act as admin permits non-admin callers (the deployed admin different from a fuzzed actor) to have different final owner, breaking the rule for some inputs.

For every caller and target address, if the original contract's deployer (admin) calls setOwner(x) then owner() equals x after the call; the mutant allows the current owner (not deployer) to call setOwner, so there exist fuzzed caller/target inputs where a non-deployer caller can change owner in the mutant but not in the reference, leading to differing owner() results.

For any caller and target address, only the original deployer (the admin, the contract creator) can successfully change owner via setOwner; the mutant lets the current owner do so, so there exist caller/target inputs where the reference keeps owner unchanged (call reverts) but the mutant allows the call and changes owner.

For every call setOwner(_owner) that completes, the reference contract always returns true (indicating success); the mutant returns false after setting owner, so it violates this property for calls that succeed.

For all callers, calling setOwner on the correct contract only succeeds (completes without revert) when the caller is the admin; the mutant removes this restriction allowing non-admin callers to succeed, so there exist callers for which the mutant succeeds but the reference reverts.
For all callers, only the admin (the deployer) can change the public owner via setOwner; the mutant removes the onlyAdmin restriction allowing non-admin callers to change owner.
